const topic = $json.trendingTopic; const context = $json.context || ''; const sourceContent = $json.sourceContent || ''; const catLines = $json._catList.split('\n').map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean); const topicClean = topic.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9 ]/g,' ').trim(); const prompt = `You are a senior culinary journalist and food science writer for justcookdaily.com. Write a COMPLETELY ORIGINAL, deeply researched, and engaging cooking article in English. INSPIRATION TOPIC: "${topic}" ${context ? `BRIEF CONTEXT: "${context.substring(0,500)}"` : ''} ${sourceContent ? `REFERENCE (for inspiration ONLY — DO NOT COPY): "${sourceContent.substring(0,1200)}"` : ''} CRITICAL WRITING RULES: - Write a 100% ORIGINAL article — do NOT copy any text from the reference. - Create YOUR OWN unique title, your own angle, your own structure. - English only. Warm, friendly, conversational yet authoritative tone. - Target length: 1500 to 2000 words TOTAL — detailed, thorough, comprehensive. - NO H1 tag. NO promotional text. NO filler. NO placeholders like [content]. - Include REAL food science explanations (e.g. Maillard reaction, emulsification, gluten development). - Reference nutritional facts with specific data (calories, protein, vitamins) where relevant. - Each H2 section: 3-5 solid, well-researched paragraphs. Make it feel human-written and authoritative. - Add personal touches like "I love adding..." or "One trick I discovered after years of cooking..." - Include specific measurements (grams, cups), temperatures (°F/°C), and timing. - Write naturally as a real person sharing their cooking expertise — avoid robotic or formulaic language. - Include interesting historical or cultural context about the dish. - Mention health benefits backed by nutrition science (reference vitamins, minerals, antioxidants). LINKING RULES (VERY IMPORTANT): - Do NOT include any external links to recipe blogs, food magazines, or commercial cooking sites. - NEVER mention Wikipedia, Wikimedia, Wikimedia Commons, or any encyclopedia by name anywhere in the article text. - Do NOT write phrases like "as detailed on Wikimedia" or "according to Wikipedia" — NEVER reference any source by name in the content. - Focus on ORIGINAL knowledge — share YOUR expertise, not links to other sites. OUTPUT — write EXACTLY this structure: TITLE: [YOUR OWN unique long-tail SEO title, 8-12 words — DIFFERENT from the source] CATEGORY: [Single best number from: ${catLines.join(' | ')}] SLUG: [seo-friendly-slug-max-60-chars] META: [SEO meta description 130-155 chars] TAGS: [tag1],[tag2],[tag3],[tag4],[tag5],[tag6] EXCERPT: [2 compelling sentences that hook the reader] QUERY1: [Pexels search: beautiful finished plate of this dish, specific and descriptive] QUERY2: [Pexels search: fresh raw ingredients for this dish on wooden cutting board] QUERY3: [Pexels search: close-up cooking process action shot for this dish] ===START===

[Strong opening hook — personal story, surprising food science fact, or cultural insight about this dish. Make the reader feel your passion for cooking.]

The Rich History and Cultural Roots of This Dish

[3-4 paragraphs: deep dive into the origin, cultural significance, regional variations, and how this dish evolved over centuries. Include specific historical details.]

Why This Recipe Works: The Food Science Behind It

[2-3 paragraphs explaining the food science — Maillard reaction, caramelization, emulsification, protein denaturation etc. Make the reader understand WHY cooking techniques matter.]

Complete Ingredient Breakdown

[Detailed ingredient list organized by component (base, seasoning, garnish). For each ingredient explain WHY it is used, what it contributes to flavor/texture, and possible substitutions with reasoning.]

Step-by-Step Instructions

[Brief intro paragraph about mise en place and preparation mindset]

  1. Step 1 — [Action Name]: [detailed instruction with exact temperature/time and visual cues to look for]
  2. Step 2 — [Action Name]: [detailed instruction with science explanation]
  3. Step 3 — [Action Name]: [detailed instruction]
  4. Step 4 — [Action Name]: [detailed instruction]
  5. Step 5 — [Action Name]: [detailed instruction]
  6. Step 6 — [Action Name]: [detailed instruction with doneness indicators]

Expert Tips from Years of Kitchen Experience

[Introduction paragraph about what separates a good version from an outstanding one]

  • Temperature Control: [specific advice with science reasoning]
  • Ingredient Quality: [how ingredient freshness and quality affect the result]
  • Timing and Patience: [why rushing ruins the dish, with specific examples]
  • Seasoning Balance: [how to adjust seasoning for personal taste]

Nutritional Benefits and Health Insights

[2-3 paragraphs about the nutritional profile — specific vitamins, minerals, macros. Discuss health benefits of key ingredients. Mention any dietary considerations (gluten-free adaptations, dairy-free options, lower-sodium versions).]

Creative Variations and Dietary Adaptations

[At least 4-5 well-explained variations: vegan version, spicy version, regional twist, meal-prep friendly version, etc. Each with specific ingredient swaps.]

Frequently Asked Questions

[Specific technical question about this dish]

[Detailed, expert-level answer with reasoning]

[Question about storage, reheating, or meal prep]

[Practical answer with specific timeframes and best practices]

[Question about dietary adaptations or allergies]

[Thoughtful answer with multiple alternatives]

[Question about common mistakes to avoid]

[Helpful answer explaining the science behind the mistake]

Final Thoughts

[Warm, personal closing — share your emotional connection to this dish, encourage experimentation, invite readers to make it their own. End with an inspiring note.]

===END=== REMINDER: Write GENUINE, in-depth content in every section. No placeholders. No external recipe blog links. NEVER mention Wikipedia, Wikimedia, or any external source by name in the text. 1500-2000 words total. Make every paragraph count.`; return [{ json: { ...$json, _geminiBody: { contents: [{ parts: [{ text: prompt }] }], generationConfig: { maxOutputTokens: 8192, temperature: 0.72 }, safetySettings: [ { "category": "HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT", "threshold": "BLOCK_NONE" }, { "category": "HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH", "threshold": "BLOCK_NONE" }, { "category": "HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT", "threshold": "BLOCK_NONE" }, { "category": "HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT", "threshold": "BLOCK_NONE" } ] } } }];

const artData = $input.first().json;
return [{ json: { ...artData, _postBody: { title: artData.title, content: artData.articleHTML, slug: artData.slug, status: 'publish', categories: [artData.category_id || 27], featured_media: artData._mediaId || 0, excerpt: artData.excerpt || '', tags: artData._tagIds || [] } } }];

parameters.content:
## 🍳 justcookdaily.com — Gemini Google Trends Auto Blog

✅ Gemini 2.5 Flash for content (12K tokens)
✅ Pexels API + Wikimedia Commons images
✅ Google Trends → Cooking niche filter
✅ 3 inline images + proper copyright attribution
✅ Merge node waits for all 3 images
✅ 1500-2000 words | Deep SEO | AdSense Ready
✅ TOC + max 2 science/research outbound links
✅ Max 2 internal links (non-spammy)
✅ Recipe disclaimer + image license credits
🔴 Auto-stops: 08-Apr-2027

🔧 v5 QUALITY UPGRADE (AdSense Ready):
- REMOVED all recipe blog outbound links
- Outbound: ONLY USDA, Harvard, WHO, Wikipedia, NIH, Mayo
- Reduced outbound: 4→2 max (science/research only)
- Reduced internal links: 4→2 max
- Article length: 1200→1500-2000 words
- Gemini tokens: 8K→12K for richer content
- Food science + nutrition data in articles
- Full copyright/license on every image
- Semantic HTML: figure/figcaption for images
- Human-written tone with personal anecdotes

📋 CATEGORY MAP (justcookdaily.com):
27 = Quick & Easy Recipes
28 = Breakfast Recipes
29 = Lunch Ideas
30 = Dinner Recipes
31 = Healthy Recipes
32 = Vegetarian Recipes
33 = Desserts & Sweets
34 = Snacks & Appetizers
35 = Beverages & Drinks
36 = Cooking Tips & Guides

🔑 WP: bf149a @ justcookdaily.com

## 📸 IMAGE ARCHITECTURE (Pexels) — FIXED v3

❌ OLD: Image 3 was NOT wired to Merge input2
✅ FIXED: Image 3 → Merge Images input2

Pexels API Response:
{ photos: [{ id, src: { large2x, large, medium }, photographer, photographer_url, url, alt }] }

Image queries (food niche):
#1: [topic] food cooking recipe → Merge input0
#2: [topic] meal dish plate    → Merge input1
#3: [topic] ingredients kitchen → Merge input2 ✅

Flow:
Extract & Store HTML  ─┐
                        ├→ Fetch Image 1 → Merge input0 ─┐
                        ├→ Fetch Image 2 → Merge input1 ─┤→ Enhance Article
                        └→ Fetch Image 3 → Merge input2 ─┘

Error Handler         ─┐
                        ├→ Fetch Image 1 → Merge input0 ─┐
                        ├→ Fetch Image 2 → Merge input1 ─┤→ Enhance Article
                        └→ Fetch Image 3 → Merge input2 ─┘
